title: Budget Allocation — Year-End Accounting
description: One week remaining. The final budget allocation of your first year in office. The numbers will be remembered.

title: Family — The Last Week
description: One week left. The residence is quieter than it was fifty-one weeks ago. But they're here. Tomas did his homework at the kitchen table tonight. Liora said 'goodnight' and meant it. Jonas made coffee for two without asking. Something survived.

title: Reelection — Final Decision
description: The party needs an answer by Friday. Your name on the ballot or not. Fifty-one weeks of governing have given you a record to run on — or a record to run from. The question is which one the voters will see.

title: All Fronts — The Final Assessment
description: Every crisis, every decision, every compromise is converging on the same week. The question is not whether you survive the convergence — it's what 'survival' means after fifty-one weeks of governing through crisis.

title: New Order — Final Assessment
description: The reform framework is largely in place. The remaining provisions will be implemented by whoever holds this office next. The question is whether that's you — and whether what you've built will survive the transition regardless.

title: Two Speeches
description: Two grey folders. VICTORY and CONCESSION. Tradition says the Chancellor writes the concession first, alone, in her own hand.
